Culīna et potūs · Kitchen, meals & drinks

cooking pot in Latin

cooking pot

caccabus (cacabus), caccabī m.

Ancient LatinQuotationsDraft
  • caccabus (cacabus), caccabī m. — cooking pot classical (M-O s.v. pan: pot (cacabus); Varro; Stat. Silv. 4.9.45)1
  • ēlixat ōllīs et cacabīs in focō — he boils in pots and pans on the hearth (Comen. OP 54)

See also: saucepan.

  1. Why caccabus, not cācabus: the word is Greek κάκκαβος, with a short α and a double κ. Varro writes caccabum (Lewis & Short), and Statius scans albōrum calicum atque caccabōrum (Silv. 4.9.45) with a heavy first syllable, which the double c explains. Lewis & Short prints cācabus, marking that heavy syllable as a long vowel. Comenius’s cacabīs is marked to match. Ruling: caccabus: a short a and a double c
